subject: Shared vs Dedicated — isolation, noisy neighbor & SLOs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — deployment mode recommendation and next steps

Hi Alex / Sara,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the deployment-mode decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and the specific isolation / SLO questions you raised.

Summary of your needs (from our notes):
- Peak QPS: ~250 rps during promos, baseline 30-650 rps
- Model: 4k-token instruction model, latency target p99 < 200ms for inference (for critical checkout paths)
- Compliance: SOC2 + limited audit logs; considering Private VPC if procurement requires network isolation
- Risk: sensitive to noisy-neighbor effects during Black Friday-style traffic bursts

Preliminary recommendation: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) looks like the best fit for predictable p99 latency and strict isolation. Hosted API can work for early integration but will need careful capacity planning to meet your p99 requirement during bursts. Private VPC is an option if your procurement/legal team requires a customer-managed network or additional KMS/HSM controls.

I attached a short one-pager that compares the three modes and our Dedicated SLA for reference (Redwood_Dedicated_SLA.pdf, deployment-options-onepager.pdf). Also attaching a simple infra/SLO diagram (infra-slos-diagram.png).

A couple of clarifying questions so we can size/pilot properly:
1) What % of requests require the full 4k context vs shorter (<=512 tokens)? This affects GPU memory and KV-cache sizing.
2) What is your expected concurrency per checkout flow (i.e., how many parallel in-flight requests per second to the same customer session)?
3) Is your procurement team likely to require a contract-level uptime SLA and a private networking option?

Next steps I propose:
- Technical follow-up (30 min) where Marissa (infra) and Vivek (solutions) join to go deeper on isolation and noisy-neighbor mitigations — can we schedule for tomorrow or Thursday?
- If Dedicated fits, we can stand up a 2-week pilot reservation with telemetry dashboards and a scoped SLA for the pilot period.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the attachments.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SLA.pdf, deployment-options-onepager.pdf, infra-slos-diagram.png

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment mode recommendation and next steps

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A few quick answers and clarifications:

- Token distribution: ~60% of requests are short (<=512), about 30% are medium (512-2k), and ~10% hit the full 4k for rare fraud-detection reviews.
- Concurrency: during peak promos we see spikes that could hit 400 concurrent inference calls for checkout validation, but most of those are short requests.
- Procurement: they will likely push for a private network option, but their legal lead wants to see cost/benefit first.

Main concern: noisy neighbor — even short latencies during peak spikes cause timeouts in our checkout flow and lead to cart abandonment. We need clarity on guarantees at p95/p99 and operational mitigations if a co-located tenant causes degradation.

Can you confirm whether Dedicated means physical GPU isolation (i.e., no other tenants on the same GPU machine) or just isolated scheduling within a shared pool? Also, what are your normal p95/p99 SLOs for our class of workload?

If you can get Marissa on a technical call to walk procurement through the isolation model and SLA guarantees, that would be great. Also please include any perf numbers you have for a 4k-token model under similar concurrency.

Alex
CTO, FinPay

Alex — thanks for the quick answers, this helps a lot. Looping in Marissa and Vivek to provide the technical details and perf numbers you requested. Below is a short overview; Marissa can expand on a call.

Short answers:
- Dedicated at Redwood means a reserved pool of GPU machines for your tenant. You get node-level isolation and scheduling controls that prevent cross-tenant preemption on the reserved pool. In practice that means other tenants will not be scheduled onto your reserved nodes.
- For noisy-neighbor mitigation in shared (hosted) pools we have runtime throttles, request prioritization, and dynamic routing to alternate model variants. For Dedicated we can configure resource reservations and runtime limits to meet p99 targets.
- Typical SLOs we commit to on Dedicated pilots: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms for similar 4k workloads (numbers depend on exact model family and batch sizes). We can run a short perf test with your payloads to validate.

Attached are a short support article and infra diagram (see attachments). For the perf numbers, Vivek — can you drop the 4k-run numbers from our last internal benchmark here so Alex has a baseline before the call?

Suggested next step: 30-min infra deep-dive tomorrow 10:00 AM PT (Marissa + Vivek + me) — does that work for you, Alex? If procurement wants a separate session on Private VPC/network + contracts we can do that in parallel.

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Shared vs Dedicated — isolation, noisy neighbor & SLOs

Hi Alex — glad to be on this thread. Quick technical summary and what we can offer for a pilot: 

1) Isolation model (Dedicated):
- Reserved GPU pools: when you reserve Dedicated capacity we provision a set of GPU nodes that are exclusively assigned to your tenant. No other customers are scheduled on those nodes.
- Node-level reservations: we can carve out GPU / memory reservations and enforce runtime limits so a single tenant job cannot exhaust the node.
- Network isolation: for Dedicated we provide private subnets and optional VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for encryption keys (this is our Private path if required).

2) Noisy-neighbor mitigations (Hosted vs Dedicated):
- Hosted: continuous batching + adaptive throttles; if a tenant exceeds thresholds we do dynamic reroute to alternate capacity and surface alarms. This works for most customers but is not absolute physical isolation.
- Dedicated: physical isolation at node level plus scheduling policies that prevent co-tenancy on reserved nodes — this eliminates classic noisy-neighbor risk coming from other tenants.

3) SLOs and pilot guarantees:
- Pilot objectives: instrumented 2-week pilot with your real traffic replay; we provision a small Dedicated pool sized to your expected peak concurrency.
- Baseline SLO targets we validate during the pilot: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms for the 4k model (we'll confirm exact numbers after a replay run).
- Monitoring: we provide dashboards with token-level latency breakdowns, per-node telemetry, and alerting tied to p95/p99 thresholds.
- Escalation: for any sustained SLA breach we offer automatic fallbacks (route to standby nodes), on-call engineering, and a postmortem within SLA windows.

4) Next practical steps:
- Schedule the infra deep-dive (we're available 10:00 AM PT tomorrow).
- If you approve, we will provision pilot Dedicated nodes for a 2-week run and run a traffic-replay test to validate p99 numbers with your payloads.

I can bring the pilot sizing template and a draft pilot SLA to the call.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
